target_question: Does Azon's preprint provide an independent level-lowering theorem that bypasses Breuil-Diamond local-lift verification?

azon_paper.author: Martin Azon
azon_paper.title: Effective Darmon's program for the generalised Fermat equation
locations_audited: Hypothesis 5: prime q' with nu_{q'} < 0, nu_{q'} not= 0 mod r, and even order mod r
Proof of Theorem 5.23: directly invokes Breuil-Diamond [BD14] Theorem 3.2.2 and BCDF25 Theorem 7.5
findings: Theorem 5.22 referenced in the paper overview corresponds to Definition 5.22 / Theorem 5.23 in the text.
For the weighted equation X^10 + 256Y^10 = Z^17, nu_q = 34*v_q(Z) - 5*v_q(UV). For every q dividing UV away from 10, nu_q is a negative multiple of 5, so nu_q mod 5 is identically 0.
Hence Hypothesis 5 fails identically for the weighted equation.
The proof of Theorem 5.23 does not develop an internal level-lowering mechanism; it cites Breuil-Diamond Theorem 3.2.2 directly.
Conclusion: Azon's work does not provide a shortcut around Breuil-Diamond Theorem 3.2.2 local-lift requirements.
